name: Dina Titus
page_title: Dina Titus' Issue Positions (Political Courage Test)
on_the_ballot: Running, Democratic for U.S. House (NV) - District 1

positions.question: Do you support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?

evidence.text: "I’ve said before that the campaign to undermine women’s reproductive freedom didn’t end when Roe was overturned. I won’t apologize for defending a woman’s right to choose, including choosing abortion medication. This ruling is out of step and dangerous."
Rated 100% by Planned Parenthood Action Fund
Voted in favor of HR 8296: "Women's Health Protection Act of 2022"
Voted in favor of HR 8297: "Ensuring Access to Abortion Act of 2022"

positions.question: Do you support expanding federal funding to support social safety net programs such as Social Security and Medicare?

evidence.text: "Over half a million individuals rely on Social Security in the State of Nevada, including 113,000 #OnlyInDistrictOne. I stand ready to work with anyone who is committed to protecting and expanding Social Security for our country’s seniors."

"We need to protect Social Security from Republican attacks. That’s a given. But I believe we can do even more. That’s why I’m supporting legislation to increase benefits by 2% on average AND fix the cost-of-living adjustment to protect our seniors from inflation."
Rated 100% by National Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare
Rated 98% by Alliance for Retired Americans

positions.question: Do you support a decrease in income taxes in order to balance the budget?

evidence.text: "I voted for the bipartisan tax bill which provides relief to families, creates affordable homes, and strengthens economic ties between the United States and Taiwan."

"Thanks to the #InflationReductionAct, which I helped pass, the IRS has recovered over $500 million without increasing audit rates on people making less than $400k per year. It’s time for wealthy tax cheats and big corporations to pay their fair share."
Rated 9% by National Taxpayers Union
Voted against HR 1: "Tax Cuts and Jobs Act"

positions.question: Do you support a wealth tax in order to pay for public programs?

evidence.text: "Thanks to the #InflationReductionAct, which I helped pass, the IRS has recovered over $500 million without increasing audit rates on people making less than $400k per year. It’s time for wealthy tax cheats and big corporations to pay their fair share."

"Tonight I spoke on the House floor to demand a #BuildBackBetter agenda that invests in families, provides a pathway to citizenship, takes action on climate, and makes the wealthy contribute their fair share."
Rated 9% by National Taxpayers Union
Voted against HR 1: "Tax Cuts and Jobs Act"

positions.question: Do you support the regulation of indirect campaign contributions from corporations, unions, and individuals?

evidence.text: Voted in favor of HR 1: "For the People Act of 2021"
"Today marks 11 years since the disastrous #CitizensUnited ruling. We must recommit to getting big money out of politics and fighting corruption in Washington."
Rated 100% by Common Cause
Rated 92% by End Citizens United

positions.question: Do you support protecting government officials, including law enforcement officers, from personal liability in civil lawsuits concerning alleged misconduct?

evidence.text: "George Floyd's death shocked the conscience of our country. It inspired millions to demand action against police brutality and systemic racism. The George Floyd Justice in Policing Act must become law."

"Today we remember George Floyd and the impact his untimely death had around the world. I applaud @POTUS’ executive order to overhaul policing so we ensure a tragedy like this one never happens again."

"You can't prevent institutional injustices with window dressing. That's why I voted to pass the bold, historic #JusticeInPolicing Act. It bans chokeholds and no-knock warrants, limits qualified immunity, and makes it easier to prosecute those who disgrace their uniform."
Voted in favor of HR 1280: "George Floyd Justice in Policing Act of 2021"

positions.question: Do you support increasing defense spending?

evidence.text: Voted in favor of HR 2670: "National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024"
Voted in favor of HR 4350: "National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022"
Voted in favor of HR 7900: "National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023"

positions.question: Do you support federal spending as a means of promoting economic growth (e.g. grants, tax incentives)?

evidence.text: "The #InflationReductionAct will create good-paying jobs, deliver the most significant action on climate in U.S. history, and dramatically reduce the deficit. Today I voted YES with every single one of my @HouseDemocrats colleagues."
Rated 5% by Council for Citizens Against Government Waste
Voted in favor of HR 1319: "American Rescue Plan Act of 2021"
Voted in favor of HR 5376: "Inflation Reduction Act of 2022"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government increasing funding for affordable housing programs?

evidence.text: "Everyone deserves a roof over their head & a safe place to live. I supported the #MinibusFunding bill to expand affordable housing options for Nevadans. I also cosponsored the #HOMEAct to address artificial hikes in rents & property costs, specifically in underserved communities."
"It’s always great to meet with the @NVARnevada to discuss affordable housing, economic development, and the federal funding I am bringing to Southern Nevada for infrastructure."

"The #BuildBackBetter Act is estimated to create, preserve, or retrofit at least 1,396,200 affordable homes and assist 867,916 households in need. I’m committed to addressing the growing disparity between housing costs & stagnant incomes for Nevadans who need it most."

positions.question: Do you support the federal government taking action, beyond those of the Federal Reserve, to alleviate inflation?

evidence.text: "Our state knows the importance of building a clean energy future while creating good-paying union jobs. Today I joined @ForOurFutureNV to discuss how the Inflation Reduction Act is supporting workers and boosting economic growth at the same time."
Voted in favor of HR 5376: "Inflation Reduction Act of 2022"
Voted in favor of HR 7688: "Consumer Fuel Price Gouging Prevention Act"

positions.question: Do you support the forgiveness of federal student loan debt?

evidence.text: "Millions of middle and working-class Americans carry the onerous burden of student debt. The President was right to veto this legislation."

"Under @POTUS’ student debt relief plan, 315,800 Nevadans are eligible for assistance, 216,900 of whom are Pell Grant recipients. This will give working and middle-class families more financial breathing room."
Rated 100% by National Education Association

positions.question: Do you support requiring a government-issued identification in order to vote at the polls?

evidence.text: "On the 58th anniversary of Bloody Sunday we remember the bravery of people like Congressman John Lewis who put their lives on the line to protect the right to vote. We must pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Act NOW."
Rated 100% by Common Cause
Voted in favor of HR 4: "John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act of 2021"
Voted in favor of HR 5746 "Freedom to Vote: John R. Lewis Act"

positions.question: Do you support a government-run (e.g. single-payer) healthcare program, such as Medicare-for-All?

evidence.text: "Before the passage of the ACA, Nevada had one of highest uninsured populations in the country. Unfortunately, on its 12th anniversary, the ACA’s still under attack by the GOP. I will continue to #ProtectOurCare because affordable healthcare is a right--not a privilege."

"Thirteen years ago today, the Affordable Care Act was signed into law by President Obama. Protestors showed up at my office after I proudly voted for the ACA. But during the following decade, Nevada's uninsured rate dropped by thirty percent. It was a big win."
Voted in favor of HR 1425: "Patient Protection and Affordable Care Enhancement Act"

positions.question: Do you support expanding paid family AND/OR medical leave benefits (e.g. maternity leave)?

evidence.text: "I’m heading back to Nevada after passing the #BuildBackBetterAct. This transformational bill will deliver investments in child care, climate action, paid family leave, expanded health care, universal pre-K, and so much more."
"Rail workers deserve paid sick leave. I look forward to voting in favor of an amendment tomorrow to provide them with this basic right."
"Today is #PaidLeave National Day of Action. As we #BuildBackBetter, we have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to pass #PaidLeaveForAll that lifts up millions of workers and families."
Voted in favor of HR 6201 "Families First Coronavirus Response Act"

positions.question: Should the government be able to regulate the cost of prescription drugs?

evidence.text: "I helped pass the Inflation Reduction Act so we could cap the cost of insulin and cut prescription drug costs. Nevadans shouldn’t have to choose between paying for their medications and putting food on the table."
"Putting people over politics means taking on the special interests and winning. When Democrats capped the cost of insulin for seniors last Congress, we beat Big Pharma. We can beat them again."
Voted in favor of HR 3 "Lower Drug Costs Now Act of 2019"
Voted in favor of HR 6833 "The Affordable Insulin Now Act"

Voted against HR 5525: "Continuing Appropriations and Border Security Enhancement Act, 2024"
